properties.description: Ruthenium on Nickel Tungsten Carbide catalyst

nodes.name: In situ hydrothermal synthesis of Ni₅₄W₇₂/rGO precursor
nodes.procedure: The precursor of Ni₅₄W₇₂/rGO was prepared by the in situ hydrothermal method, and the composition and morphology were characterized (detailed preparation in Supporting Information, Figures S8 and S9). The POM of Ni₅₄W₇₂ (Figure S7) was selected as starting material.
nodes.source_text: The precursor of Ni₅₄W₇₂/rGO was prepared by the in situ hydrothermal method, and the composition and morphology were characterized (Figures S8 and S9, Supporting Information).

nodes.name: Impregnation and drying of Ru precursor
nodes.procedure: 1.8 mL of an aqueous solution RuCl₃·3H₂O (10 mg mL⁻¹) was added to a small beaker containing 0.3 g Ni₅₄W₇₂/rGO and 5 mL H₂O and dispersed the mixture well with magnetic stirring for 3 h, then heated at 90°C until dry and cooling in the ambient to produce a solid mixture powder.

nodes.name: Grinding with phosphazene and two-stage pyrolysis
nodes.procedure: The resulting dry solid mixture was well-ground with 3.75 mg N₃Cl₆P₃ and pyrolyzed in tube furnace under pure N₂ flow: temperature raised to 500°C at 2°C min⁻¹ for 20 min, then to 650°C at 5°C min⁻¹ and held for 6 h, then cooled to ambient temperature. During pyrolysis, Ni₅₄W₇₂/rGO polymerized with N₃Cl₆P₃, followed by RuCl₃ reduction and Ni₅₄W₇₂ deoxygenation, resulting in Ru/Ni/WC core with N,P-co-doped carbon nanolayers.

nodes.characterization_summary: EDS elemental mapping shows Ru, Ni, W with certain segregation but overlapping distribution, confirming complex dispersed Ru/Ni/WC multi-interface structure.
nodes.evidence_snippet: EDS elemental mapping was executed to examine further the presence of Ru, Ni, W, C, N, and P in one Ru/Ni/WC@NPC nanoparticle (Figure 2d-j). Elemental mapping reveals that the distribution of Ru, Ni, and W exhibits certain segregation (Figure 2e-g), but they overlap and interweave with each other (Figure 2h).

nodes.evidence_snippet: XRD analysis (Figure 3a) was accomplished to define the composition of Ru/Ni/WC@NPC (Ru wt.% = 4.13%). The diffraction peaks appeared at 38.37° (100), 42.10° (002), 43.73° (101), 58.18° (102), 69.41° (110), and 78.38° (103) are corresponded to planes of metallic Ru (JCPDS: 06-0663), respectively.

nodes.characterization_summary: Type IV isotherm with H3 hysteresis loop indicating mesoporous structure. BET surface area of 114.99 m²/g.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The nitrogen sorption isotherms, specific surface areas, and pore nanostructures of Ru/Ni/WC@NPC (Ru wt.% = 4.13%) and Ni/WC@NPC electrocatalysts were determined using Brunauer-Emmett-Teller (BET). ... the BET surface area of Ru/Ni/WC@ NPC (Ru wt.% = 4.13%) is nearly identical to that of Ni/WC@ NPC, signifying that the addition of Ru did not cause aggregation of the material. Such an extensive specific surface area (114.99 m² g⁻¹)...

nodes.characterization_summary: G band at 1585 cm⁻¹ and D band at 1353 cm⁻¹ with I_D/I_G ratio of 1.06, verifying disordered carbon.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The existence of carbon in the Ru/Ni/WC@NPC (Ru wt.% = 4.13%) catalyst was investigated using the Raman spectrum. Figure S18, Supporting Information presents the G and D bands that appeared at 1585 and 1353 cm⁻¹, with an intensity (I_D / I_G) ratio of 1.06, verifying the disorder of carbon in this composite material.
